dispatch.summary:
I'm approving T415 (91d2f6c0 against fe1508d3). It meets every acceptance item and changes no engine or web code. I didn't run any tests myself because this review session is read-only. The runner's own check passed: typecheck, lint, format:check and `vitest --changed` (98 files, 810 tests), all under the default config. The worker reports that worlds.test.ts also passes (4 tests) under the release-on config; the runner didn't run that, and I checked it by reading the code instead.

The risk reason was the autopilot decision of 2026-10-24 that is still waiting for the owner: every test names its release, and a release-on vitest config checks each file with the switch both on and off. The change follows that decision exactly, adds no new planning decisions, and only touches test setup, so it doesn't lock out the alternatives.

What I checked in the code:
- `DISABLED_RELEASE` and `ENABLED_RELEASE` are copies of the release object, so they keep their own on/off value whatever the switch is.
- `simulatedWorld(input, span, release = MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE)` puts the release in its cache ID and passes it through every nested build. The engine only reads the release in `createWorld` and the host constructor, and season rollover never reads it, so a world built with a given release stays on that release.
- `cached` reads `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` when it runs and adds it to the key for both the memory and the disk cache.
- The engine's release object isn't frozen, and the setup file and the tests import the same object.
- `vitest.release-on.config.ts` merges the base config, which has no setupFiles, workspaces or projects. The tsconfig includes root `*.ts` files and allows `.ts` imports. The `package.json` script matches the acceptance text exactly.
- The cache-separation test flips the switch inside one case and restores it in `finally`. That is safe because cases in a file run one after another and the base config keeps each file in its own worker. The task notes say only the setup file should change the switch; this test-only flip goes beyond that, but the worker disclosed it, it is scoped to one case, and it proves the separation within a single run.

There are two optional suggestions and nothing that needs fixing.

findings.message: The global `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` goes into every cache key, including `simulatedWorld` calls that pass an explicit release. Those worlds don't depend on the global switch, so the switch-off and release-on runs can't share them. That includes the `DISABLED_RELEASE` worlds that T417 will use for most shared engine worlds. Running both test tiers therefore builds and stores each of these worlds twice, which matters given the known problem of the world cache filling the disk. This follows the acceptance as written and doesn't affect T420's cold-vs-cold gate. Optional, for T420 to weigh against its warm timings: hash the effective release instead, i.e. the explicit one for `simulatedWorld` and the default for `cachedWorld`.

The test "simulatedWorld pins the release it is given" only covers a world on its founding day. If the release were dropped from the nested `simulatedWorld(…, release)` calls for seasons or rounds, the default would quietly take over, and none of the tests would catch it under either config. Optional: add a cheap case such as `simulatedWorld(input, { rounds: 1 }, DISABLED_RELEASE).matchModel` toBeUndefined, which fails under the release-on config if the release isn't passed down.

dispatch.summary:
I fixed `season.settle.test.ts` and added the new case, but I'm returning blocked on one point. Acceptance item 1 asks for a case that "fails on the unfixed source", and that can't hold: no engine path writes an invalid record in an activated world.

**What the probe actually hit.** I reran the file with the release switch on and got the same 5 failures. Every one threw in `recordMatch` (`season.ts:290`) on fixture 1950:ENG:4:0:0:0. Each record had already passed the same check in `simulateMatch` (`match.ts:553`) before the test changed it. The test's own edits broke the records:
- Replacing the incidents dropped the grid's two cautions ("cards ≠ incidents").
- Injury and red incidents left the player on 90 minutes.
- The substitute case added a line built from `zeroMetrics()` with no advanced counters ("advanced counters missing"), in 1950, when no substitutes are allowed.
- The fatigue case set 45 minutes with no exit.

Every activated path checks its record where it is written, and `recordMatch` checks again. Two whole activated seasons settled with no error:
- **1950 world, release on:** 46 rounds plus the close, 31 own matches, 12.0 s, every own record carrying the model and per-player counters.
- **2024 world, release on:** league, cups, Europe and playoff, 20.4 s. I ran this as a temporary test file and deleted it.

I changed no engine code, and the validator is untouched. It reads 1950 cautions correctly.

**Changes in the test file:**
- Every world now takes an explicit release.
- New case "an activated world settles only valid full records": the 1950 world with the release on settles its league's first two rounds (own match in the detailed engine, the rest on the aggregate path) and the English cup's first round. Every record passes `validateFullMatchRecord`, including at least one extra-time record and one shoot-out.
- The injury, NPC injury and ban cases now run with the release on. Their helper adds one incident and keeps the record consistent: incidents stay in minute order, a red card counts on the player and team, and the player's minutes stop at the incident. The grid's own incidents are kept. The ban case now checks that the sent-off player's ban was served, instead of clearing the next match's incidents.
- The substitute and fatigue cases moved to a 2024 world on the new model and read real substitutions and real minutes. No case needed the disabled release.

**Checks:**
- The settle file passes under both configs: 6 of 6 each, against 5 failures before with the release on.
- typecheck, lint and format:check pass, and `vitest run --changed` against base 2737e84a passes (1 file, 6 tests).
- Not run here: the batch tier (`test:unit`, `test:contract`, `validate:catalogs`, `build`, Chromium playwright) is left to the unit gate. The whole release-on unit tier is T420's job.

Item 1 is left unchecked; items 2–4 are checked. The result section of the task file has the full evidence. Two shell commands were refused by the permission check and not retried: the haeram CLI's `vibe format` read and one command using a shell variable. I re-ran the checks without the variable.

T417 (ce152a9b vs 2737e84a) is approved. All twelve touched files now found every world under DISABLED_RELEASE. Five call createWorld(input, DISABLED_RELEASE) directly; the gridKit callers pass gridKit(tactics, seed, DISABLED_RELEASE). DISABLED_RELEASE is exactly the current off switch ({revision, enabled:false}), so the default run's behaviour cannot change and no expectation or digest was edited. Engine source reads the release default only in createWorld, the host and the testkit default, and none of the twelve files reaches any of those now. Their release-on behaviour is therefore identical to switch-off by construction, which agrees with the worker's reported release-on run (167 passed; the before-run's 55 failures match the listed per-file counts). The candidate cases still opt in deliberately through the setup's model (engine.test `candidate`, playback.test's candidate flag, shape/coordination/state model overrides), so no case is on both paths by accident. The first risk reason, the change outside touches in grid/testkit.ts, is disclosed in limits and minimal: one optional `release` parameter whose default is the same as before. It overlaps no sibling lane's touches (T416/T418/T419). For the second risk reason, the only coordinator decision on the board concerns T416, and T417's result makes no provisional planning decision. No engine source was changed. Host verification ran typecheck, lint, format:check and `vitest run --changed` (17 files, 227 passed). I did not re-run the release-on probe: this checkout has no node_modules, and installing them would modify the read-only review workspace, so that run rests on the worker's record plus the static argument above.

dispatch.summary:
T415 구현을 마쳤습니다. 커밋과 제출은 호스트 러너 몫으로 남겨 두었습니다. 엔진과 웹 코드는 손대지 않았습니다.

변경 내용:
- `tests/fixtures/worlds.ts`: `ENABLED_RELEASE` 옆에 `DISABLED_RELEASE`를 추가했습니다. `simulatedWorld(input, span, release = MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE)`는 받은 release를 `createWorld`와 하위 시즌/라운드 빌드까지 넘기고, 캐시 id에도 붙입니다. `cached`는 호출 시점의 `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled`를 모든 캐시 키에 넣으므로, 스위치를 끈 채 만든 월드가 스위치를 켠 실행에 쓰이지 않습니다. 기존 디스크 캐시는 한 번씩 다시 빌드됩니다.
- `tests/setup/release-on.ts`: 엔진의 `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled`를 켭니다. readonly 캐스트는 이 setup 파일에만 둡니다.
- `vitest.release-on.config.ts`: `vitest.config.ts`를 merge하고 위 setup 파일을 추가합니다.
- `package.json`: `test:unit:release-on` 스크립트를 추가했습니다.
- `tests/fixtures/worlds.test.ts`: "simulatedWorld pins the release it is given"과 "the world cache separates the default release" 두 테스트를 추가했습니다.

검증 결과:
- typecheck, lint, format:check 모두 통과했습니다.
- worlds.test.ts는 기본 config와 release-on config에서 각각 4개 모두 통과했습니다.
- setup 파일이 실제로 스위치를 켜는지 따로 확인했습니다. `match-model.test.ts`의 "keeps production activation off"가 release-on에서는 실패하고(`enabled: true`) 기본 config에서는 통과합니다.
- `vitest run --changed fe1508d3`를 8개 shard로 나눠 돌려 98개 파일, 810개 테스트가 모두 통과했습니다. 대상은 worlds.ts를 import하는 파일 전부입니다.

남은 일과 참고 사항:
- release-on 전체 실행(`pnpm run test:unit:release-on`)은 impl notes 지시대로 돌리지 않았습니다. T416–T419 레인이 자기 파일을 맞추고 T420이 전체를 잴 때까지는 실패가 예상됩니다.
- 캐시 분리 테스트는 한 번의 실행만으로 분리를 증명하려고, 그 테스트 하나 안에서 스위치를 잠깐 뒤집었다가 `finally`에서 되돌립니다. impl notes의 "캐스트는 setup 파일에만" 문구를 엄격히 읽으면 벗어나는 부분이라 task result limits에 적어 두었습니다. 실행 전체에 걸쳐 스위치를 켜는 건 여전히 setup 파일뿐입니다.
- 묶음 관문 검사(test:unit, test:contract, validate:catalogs, build, Chromium playwright)는 unit 관문에 맡겼습니다.

실제로 돌린 검사와 남긴 항목은 task result에 그대로 적었습니다.

dispatch.summary:
T421 is done. At 1x a match minute now takes 12 real seconds (`WATCH_MINUTE_MS` = 12000), and every match opens at 2x (`WATCH_DEFAULT_SPEED` = 2 in `presentationClock.ts`). `Pitch.tsx` starts at that speed and resets to it whenever a new match record loads, so live watching and archived replays both open with the 2x chip selected.

Unit tests:
- The clock tests now include "1x lasts 12 s a match minute" and "matches open at 2x".
- The goal-feedback and possession-cue tests read `WATCH_MINUTE_MS` instead of assuming 4 s minutes. The possession test's offsets had relied on 4 s and would otherwise have failed.
- The goal hold is still 1 real second at every speed, and the existing speed-change cases pass.

Checks that passed: the 3 affected test files (30 tests), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`, `vitest run --changed fe1508d3` (4 files, 42 tests) and `pnpm run build`. I did not run any browser specs; they wait for the batch run.

Browser specs updated to take their waits from the constants:
- In touches: `stable-controls-and-pacing.spec.ts` and `tests/fixtures/full-model-continuity.ts`.
- Outside touches, because the 2x default or the slower 16x minute (now 750 ms) would break them: `full-model-continuity.spec.ts` (the timing is in the spec, not the fixture), `match-core.spec.ts` and `mobile-match-presentation.spec.ts`. No other open task touches these files, and T286 depends on T422, so I see no clash. The scope check may still flag them.

Things to know before the batch run:
- `set-piece-defence.spec.ts` is unchanged. It only jumps to paused moments and has no timed waits; T422 adds its set-piece assertions.
- Journeys that watch a whole match at 16x now spend about 72 s watching instead of 24 s. Their timeouts and test time limits were raised to match.
- All of this is written in the task result's limits.

dispatch.summary:
T417 is done: all twelve touched test files now pass with the release switch both off and on (167 tests each way). With the switch on, they had 55 failures before the change, matching the per-file counts in the task.

What changed (test code only, no engine source):
- Every world in the twelve files is now built with `DISABLED_RELEASE`. Each case tests how the pre-feature path works, and the candidate cases already switch to the new model per fixture by setting `model: MATCH_MODEL_REVISION` on the setup.
- No case was moved to candidate expectations, no expectation or recorded digest changed, and no case needed a source change, so none is left for T420.
- Where a file calls `createWorld` directly (engine, playback, state, record's 60-match case, summary), it now passes `DISABLED_RELEASE` as the second argument.
- Where a file gets its world from `gridKit` (decide, record, shape, resolve, intentions, restarts, coordination, portable-math), the call is now `gridKit(tactics, seed, DISABLED_RELEASE)`.

One edit is outside the task's touches: `packages/engine/src/grid/testkit.ts`. Eight of the twelve files get their world only through `gridKit`, so there was no other way for them to name a release short of copying the kit builder. `gridKit` now takes an optional third `release` argument whose default is the same as `createWorld`'s, so its other users behave exactly as before. FORMAT's review policy sends this unit to review because of that file. The five other `gridKit` users (discipline, tags, movement, shootout, aggregate/engine tests) pass with the switch both ways (60 tests) but don't name a release yet. T420 or T419 may pin them.

Checks run:
- typecheck, lint and format:check passed.
- `vitest run --changed 2737e84a7471 --passWithNoTests` ran 17 files (the twelve plus the five other `gridKit` users), and all 227 tests passed.

Acceptance item 1 requires the new case to fail on the unfixed source, which can't happen without such a bug. How should T416 close?

dispatch.summary:
I fixed `season.settle.test.ts` and added the new case, but I'm returning blocked on one point. Acceptance item 1 asks for a case that "fails on the unfixed source", and that can't hold: no engine path writes an invalid record in an activated world.

**What the probe actually hit.** I reran the file with the release switch on and got the same 5 failures. Every one threw in `recordMatch` (`season.ts:290`) on fixture 1950:ENG:4:0:0:0. Each record had already passed the same check in `simulateMatch` (`match.ts:553`) before the test changed it. The test's own edits broke the records:
- Replacing the incidents dropped the grid's two cautions ("cards ≠ incidents").
- Injury and red incidents left the player on 90 minutes.
- The substitute case added a line built from `zeroMetrics()` with no advanced counters ("advanced counters missing"), in 1950, when no substitutes are allowed.
- The fatigue case set 45 minutes with no exit.

Every activated path checks its record where it is written, and `recordMatch` checks again. Two whole activated seasons settled with no error:
- **1950 world, release on:** 46 rounds plus the close, 31 own matches, 12.0 s, every own record carrying the model and per-player counters.
- **2024 world, release on:** league, cups, Europe and playoff, 20.4 s. I ran this as a temporary test file and deleted it.

I changed no engine code, and the validator is untouched. It reads 1950 cautions correctly.

**Changes in the test file:**
- Every world now takes an explicit release.
- New case "an activated world settles only valid full records": the 1950 world with the release on settles its league's first two rounds (own match in the detailed engine, the rest on the aggregate path) and the English cup's first round. Every record passes `validateFullMatchRecord`, including at least one extra-time record and one shoot-out.
- The injury, NPC injury and ban cases now run with the release on. Their helper adds one incident and keeps the record consistent: incidents stay in minute order, a red card counts on the player and team, and the player's minutes stop at the incident. The grid's own incidents are kept. The ban case now checks that the sent-off player's ban was served, instead of clearing the next match's incidents.
- The substitute and fatigue cases moved to a 2024 world on the new model and read real substitutions and real minutes. No case needed the disabled release.

**Checks:**
- The settle file passes under both configs: 6 of 6 each, against 5 failures before with the release on.
- typecheck, lint and format:check pass, and `vitest run --changed` against base 2737e84a passes (1 file, 6 tests).
- Not run here: the batch tier (`test:unit`, `test:contract`, `validate:catalogs`, `build`, Chromium playwright) is left to the unit gate. The whole release-on unit tier is T420's job.

Item 1 is left unchecked; items 2–4 are checked. The result section of the task file has the full evidence. Two shell commands were refused by the permission check and not retried: the haeram CLI's `vibe format` read and one command using a shell variable. I re-ran the checks without the variable.

review.summary: T417 (ce152a9b vs 2737e84a) is approved. All twelve touched files now found every world under DISABLED_RELEASE. Five call createWorld(input, DISABLED_RELEASE) directly; the gridKit callers pass gridKit(tactics, seed, DISABLED_RELEASE). DISABLED_RELEASE is exactly the current off switch ({revision, enabled:false}), so the default run's behaviour cannot change and no expectation or digest was edited. Engine source reads the release default only in createWorld, the host and the testkit default, and none of the twelve files reaches any of those now. Their release-on behaviour is therefore identical to switch-off by construction, which agrees with the worker's reported release-on run (167 passed; the before-run's 55 failures match the listed per-file counts). The candidate cases still opt in deliberately through the setup's model (engine.test `candidate`, playback.test's candidate flag, shape/coordination/state model overrides), so no case is on both paths by accident. The first risk reason, the change outside touches in grid/testkit.ts, is disclosed in limits and minimal: one optional `release` parameter whose default is the same as before. It overlaps no sibling lane's touches (T416/T418/T419). For the second risk reason, the only coordinator decision on the board concerns T416, and T417's result makes no provisional planning decision. No engine source was changed. Host verification ran typecheck, lint, format:check and `vitest run --changed` (17 files, 227 passed). I did not re-run the release-on probe: this checkout has no node_modules, and installing them would modify the read-only review workspace, so that run rests on the worker's record plus the static argument above.

findings.message: gridKit gained an optional `release` parameter (default MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE), which is outside T417's touches. It is needed so the eight kit-only files can name a release, the default is unchanged, and the result's limits disclose it. No fix needed; noted so the integrator knows the touches list was exceeded on purpose.

The other five gridKit users still read the switch's default. They pass under both states today, but T420's acceptance only fixes files that are still failing, so after T286 flips the switch these files would quietly move to the candidate path. Planning (T420 owner) should decide whether they pin a release explicitly. This is not a T417 defect.
